key_insight: MedMO is a medical multimodal LLM trained end-to-end on large-scale, domain-specific data with a multi‑stage recipe that aligns visual encoders to a medical language backbone, enabling grounded understanding and reasoning over medical images.
problem_solved: Bridges gaps in domain coverage, modality alignment, and grounded reasoning that limit the adoption of general MLLMs in clinical and medical-image understanding tasks.
method: Cross-modal pretraining to align heterogeneous visual encoders with a medical language backbone (stage i from the paper).
Large-scale, domain-specific image–text pretraining and targeted fine-tuning on medical corpora to improve medical coverage and modality-specific representations.
Grounding and reasoning training (instruction/contrastive style tuning and/or grounding modules) to produce grounded, clinically relevant explanations and decisions from images.
impact: Provides a foundation MLLM tailored for medical images that improves reliability and interpretability of image-based answers — enabling researchers and practitioners to build safer, better-grounded clinical AI assistants and diagnostic tools.
visual_elements: Multi-stage training pipeline diagram (cross-modal pretraining → domain fine-tuning → grounding/reasoning).
Architecture overview showing visual encoders, medical language backbone, and alignment layers/connectors.
Example case panel: medical image with model attention/heatmap overlays plus generated grounded explanation.
Benchmark chart comparing MedMO vs. baselines on grounding, accuracy, and explanation faithfulness metrics.
paper_title: MedMO: Grounding and Understanding Multimodal Large Language Model for Medical Images
paper_authors: Ankan Deria, Komal Kumar, Adinath Madhavrao Dukre, Eran Segal, Salman Khan
